# rviuer

The goal of rviuer is to provide a tool to show the plot in R session (and to practice my Rust coding 🦀). 

## Installation

You can install the development version of rviuer from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Exceret/rviuer")
```

## Usage

The package works in two steps: `capture_plot()` turns plotting code into PNG bytes, and `render_plot()` prints those bytes (or an image file) in the terminal.

```{r}
#| label = "usage_capture",
#| eval = FALSE
library(rviuer)

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point()
capture_plot(p, width = 6, height = 4) |> render_plot()
```

`capture_plot()` evaluates the plotting code on an in-memory `ragg` device, so no temporary file is created; a visible return value is printed automatically, which is why a `ggplot` object can be passed directly. Base graphics draw on the device as usual, and any output format works:

```{r}
#| label = "usage_base_graphics",
#| eval = FALSE
capture_plot(plot(1:10), width = 4, height = 3) |> render_plot()

capture_plot(
  {
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    hist(rnorm(100))
    boxplot(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars)
  },
  width = 8,
  height = 3
) |>
  render_plot()
```

### Render an image file

`render_plot()` also accepts a path, and any format the `image` crate can decode is fine.

```{r}
#| label = "usage_file_path",
#| eval = FALSE
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidyverse/dplyr/main/man/figures/logo.png"
dest <- file.path(tempdir(), "logo.png")

download.file(url, destfile = dest, mode = "wb")
render_plot(dest)
```

### Control the size

Two independent sizes are involved, and confusing them is the usual surprise:

- `capture_plot(width, height, units, res)` sets the physical size of the captured PNG (inches, cm, mm or px).
- `get_viuer_config(width, height)` sets how many **terminal cells** the image occupies.

```{r}
#| label = "usage_size",
#| eval = FALSE
# sharp image, 60 columns wide on screen
capture_plot(p, width = 8, height = 5) |>
  render_plot(get_viuer_config(width = 60))
```

When both config dimensions are `NULL` (the default) the image is fitted to the terminal, keeping the aspect ratio and never scaling a small image up. Setting only one of them lets the other follow from the aspect ratio.

### Other options

`get_viuer_config()` collects the printing options: size, offsets (`x`, `y`, `absolute_offset`), `transparent` and `premultiplied_alpha` for images with alpha, `restore_cursor` for redrawing in place, and `truecolor`, `use_iterm`, `use_kitty`, `use_sixel` to allow or forbid a graphics protocol.

```{r}
#| label = "usage_config",
#| eval = FALSE
render_plot(
  "logo.png",
  config = get_viuer_config(width = 40, transparent = TRUE)
)
```

### Pixel art text

`draw_pixels()` renders text with the built-in 3 x 5 font and returns a `ggplot` object, so it can be extended or saved like any other plot.

```{r}
#| label = "usage_pixel_art",
#| eval = FALSE
draw_pixels("rviuer")
draw_pixels("rviuer", color_by = "letter")
draw_pixels("hello\nworld", fill = "tomato", border = NA)

draw_pixels("rviuer") |>
  capture_plot(width = 6, height = 2) |>
  render_plot()
```

The font covers `A`-`Z`, `0`-`9`, the space and a few punctuation marks; missing characters can be added with `pixel_font_add()`. `text_to_matrix()` and `matrix_to_pixels()` expose the underlying pixel grid.

```{r}
#| label = "usage_pixel_font",
#| eval = FALSE
font <- pixel_font_add(
  pixel_font_3x5,
  "#",
  c("101", "111", "101", "111", "101")
)
draw_pixels("C#", font = font, palette = c("tomato", "steelblue"))
```

### Where images can be shown

The graphics protocol is chosen automatically: iTerm, Kitty or Sixel when the terminal supports it, coloured half-blocks otherwise. A real terminal is required — RStudio, Positron and other IDE consoles, `Rscript` with redirected output and CI logs only receive the fallback's escape sequences. Use `isatty(stdout())` (or `interactive()`) to guard rendering code in scripts.

## Agent skill

The repository ships an agent skill in `skills/rviuer/`, so coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy, ...) know how to drive the package: the capture/render pipeline, the difference between a capture size and a terminal-cell size, which protocol the current terminal gets, and the error messages worth recognising. It also bundles `skills/rviuer/scripts/check_terminal.R`, which reports the detected protocol, the terminal size and an optional test render.

Install it with the `skills` CLI:

``` bash
npx skills add Exceret/rviuer --skill rviuer
```

From a local clone the same command works with the path instead of the repository name:

``` bash
npx skills add . --skill rviuer
```

Add `--list` to only show the skills a repository offers, `--global` to install at user level instead of project level, and `--copy` to copy the files rather than symlink them into the agent directory.
